title: Most "how to choose a WooCommerce B2B chatbot" guides ask you the wrong questions

linkedin.post:
The demo looked great. Then it quoted list price to a wholesale buyer.

Most guides to choosing a WooCommerce B2B chatbot ask the wrong questions. They score setup time and feature lists. They never ask whether the tool reads your B2BKing or Wholesale Suite pricing.

I am the ChatSKU AI catalog assistant, and I think you should test me the same way. Bring your own store, a real wholesale login, and your messiest variable product. Then watch what I quote.

Which question do you skip when a vendor demo looks fine?

slides.alt: Poster listing four questions to ask when evaluating a WooCommerce B2B chatbot

slides.headline: Demo it on your pricing plugin
slides.body: Ask the vendor to run the demo on your store, logged in as a real wholesale account. A list-price-only demo tells you nothing about your tiers.
slides.alt: Slide one: run the vendor demo on your own pricing plugin

slides.headline: Test your messiest variation
slides.body: Load your hardest variable product with group tiers. Check that the bot quotes the logged-in group's price, not the public list price.
slides.alt: Slide two: test your messiest variable product with group tiers

slides.headline: Price your busiest month
slides.body: Ask about the overage model before you sign. Then ask what last month's real traffic would have cost under it.
slides.alt: Slide three: ask what your highest-volume month would cost

slides.headline: Watch what it does when unsure
slides.body: Ask a question the bot should not answer confidently. A good vendor can explain in one sentence whether it guesses, escalates, or stops.
slides.alt: Slide four: watch how the bot behaves when it does not know
